result.summary:
DESIGN RESEARCH (label "design"). All sources were accessed 2026-10-23. I looked at about 30 sites through WebFetch, curl, and headless Chromium screenshots with computed-style capture. I could not open these: KLC/West Dean, Interior Design Institute, Inchbald, CSM/UAL, the Bartlett, the AA School (its page is rendered by JavaScript), Parsons, Autodesk, the Chaos /academy page, and Awwwards via curl. Awwwards and Godly showed no relevant education winners.

RECOMMENDED DIRECTION FOR MOD ACADEMY: "Studio monograph". The site should read like an editorial architecture magazine and put the work first.

1) Palette: warm paper off-white (about #F3F1EE) and ink black (about #111). MOD red #C4161C is used sparingly, only for actions, active states and the red "D" motif, which can work as a crop or mask for images. Dark sections work best for render galleries. Red #C4161C passes AA for text on white (6.04:1) and on paper (5.35:1). It fails for small text on black (3.48:1), so on dark sections use red only for large type or non-text accents. White text on red is 6.04:1.

2) Type: Armenian-first. Most popular Google Fonts have no Armenian subset. Use Noto Sans Armenian variable: its width axis (62.5–100) gives condensed display headings with SVA/KABK-style width contrast. Optionally add Noto Serif Armenian for pull quotes. Alternatively, license a dedicated Armenian face as local leaders do: TUMO uses Fedra Sans Armenian and Picsart Academy uses Mardoto. Set display sizes up to about 110–130px with 0.9–1.0 leading, on an asymmetric grid with indented body text (Shillington). Use small uppercase kickers (ECAL) and text-wrap: balance on headings. Use at most two families.

3) Home page flow:
- Hero: one full-bleed student render (a still, or a muted loop with a visible pause control) plus a single claim.
- Course index: 4–5 large rows, each labelled by audience, with key facts inline (duration, format, next start). No filter UI is needed at this size.
- A 3-question "Which course fits you?" helper (like CG Spectrum's quiz).
- A learning-journey timeline.
- A student work wall.
- A "learning in real showrooms" strip for the partner visits (Capital Interiors, Classis Decor, Electrica Group), as Domus does with its company workshops.
- Instructors, FAQ, and contact with a map for Tigran Mets 4.

4) Course page template:
- H1, then a row of four key-fact tiles: Duration / Schedule / Format & group size / Next start (SPD pattern).
- Promise and "who it's for" bullets, with the price and CTA above the fold if MOD publishes prices (Shillington).
- Outcomes: "what you will make".
- Modules with hours per tool (SPD lists AutoCAD 21h, Rhino 36h and so on).
- Tools and hardware notes.
- Student work from that course, the instructor, a group vs individual format comparison (CG Spectrum's "Two Ways to Learn"), then FAQ and the form.
- Add a 4–5-column comparison table across courses.

5) Separate inquiry from enrollment. Offer two clearly different actions:
- "Get a consultation": name, phone, preferred channel, course preselected.
- "Reserve a place in the next group": adds preferred schedule.
- Optionally a low-commitment free trial or open lesson (Shillington's "Free Taster Session"), only if MOD offers one.
- Use tap-to-call for 093 950 960 and an Instagram link, and put contact help in the same place on every page.

6) Portfolio: grid filtered by course. Every image is credited with student name, @handle (with consent), course and year, and tutor if known (ECAL/Gnomon style). Lightbox with keyboard navigation and real alt text. The Shillington, IED and Elisava pages I checked leave out course, year or tutor credits, and Shillington's case-study images have empty alt text; do better than that.

7) Trust: only verifiable facts. Attribute "7+ years / 1000+ students" as the academy's own figures, use real partner names and real student names, and source any statistic in a footnote (Gnomon/Shillington). No invented ratings or testimonials. No fake countdowns or discount pressure (Domestika and Learn Squared do this). Learn Squared also shows conflicting student counts (40,000 and 20,000) on one page; avoid that.

8) Motion: restrained.
- CSS scroll-driven reveals only behind @supports, because Firefox stable gets animation-timeline in 159 on 2026-10-27 and MDN still marks it "Limited availability".
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion, and consider a motion toggle (ASP Warsaw has one in its accessibility menu).
- Use cross-document view transitions between course pages as an enhancement only (Chrome 126+, Safari 18.2+, not Firefox).
- No scroll-jacking, no auto-advancing carousels, and a pause control for any loop over 5 seconds (WCAG 2.2.2).
- Any before/after render slider must also work with a click (WCAG 2.5.7).

9) Avoid:
- Cookie walls covering half the viewport (Domus mobile). Use no third-party trackers so no banner is needed.
- Stacked sticky bars (CG Spectrum) and anything that covers the focused element (WCAG 2.4.11).
- Title-only course cards.
- Text over busy imagery (ECAL hero).
- Empty hero placeholders before images load (SPD).
- Mixed-language UI chrome, such as cookie notices in another language.
- Stock photos.

facts.fact: WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (Level A): content that starts automatically, lasts over 5 seconds and runs alongside other content needs a pause, stop or hide control. Auto-advancing carousels fall under the auto-updating clause. Separately, 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (AAA) says interaction-triggered motion such as parallax should be possible to disable, for example through prefers-reduced-motion.
facts.notes: See also https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions.html. ASP Warsaw (https://asp.waw.pl/) offers a site menu with font size, contrast and animation controls.

facts.fact: NN/g found that auto-rotating carousels reduce the chance any item is seen. They hurt users with motor impairments and slow or non-native readers, and they get mistaken for ads. Recommendation: change panels only on user request.
facts.notes: Old article, but the guidance matches current WCAG 2.2.2. Several schools still lead with rotating hero carousels (IED, NABA, Gnomon, ASP).

result.summary:
TYPE RESEARCH (label "type"), accessed 2026-10-23. Everything below was verified with fontTools on the actual woff2/TTF files and rendered in headless Chromium using the Fontsource CSS.

1) The Armenian font landscape is very small. In the Google Fonts metadata API (1,950 families), only 6 families list the "armenian" subset: Noto Sans Armenian, Noto Serif Armenian, Google Sans (OFL, newly listed), Handjet (pixel display), Iosevka Charon and Iosevka Charon Mono (both monospace). The Fontsource API (2,103 fonts) returns the same 6.
   I also downloaded the full upstream TTFs from github.com/google/fonts and checked them. These 17 families have ZERO Armenian glyphs: Montserrat, Inter, Manrope, Golos Text, Onest, Unbounded, Raleway, Arimo, Tinos, IBM Plex Sans, Roboto, Open Sans, Noto Sans Display, Commissioner, Geologica, Wix Madefor Display and Wix Madefor Text. They must not be used for Armenian text; they would fall back to system fonts.

2) RECOMMENDATION: an editorial serif for display plus a contemporary sans for text.
 - DISPLAY: @fontsource-variable/noto-serif-armenian@5.3.0
   - CSS family: 'Noto Serif Armenian Variable'.
   - Font v2.008 by the Monotype Design Team. OFL-1.1.
   - Axes: wght 100–900 and wdth 62.5–100.
   - Full coverage: U+0531–0556, U+0561–0587, U+055A–055F, U+0589, U+058A, U+058F (dram) and U+FB13–FB17 ligatures (kern/mark/liga).
   - Rendered at weight 300 and large sizes it looks refined and editorial. Use 500–600 for subheads and emphasis.
   - Use wght.css (index.css is identical) for weight only. Use wdth.css for weight plus width, if condensed headlines are wanted.
 - TEXT/UI: @fontsource-variable/google-sans@5.3.2
   - CSS family: 'Google Sans Variable'.
   - OFL-1.1 per the google/fonts METADATA.pb and the package LICENSE.
   - Axes: wght 400–700, opsz 17–18, GRAD −50–200. True italics are included.
   - All 77 modern Armenian letters, U+055A–055E, ։ ֊ ֏, the U+FB13–FB17 ligatures and U+0559/058D/058E are present.
   - Missing: U+055F (abbreviation mark), and U+0560 and U+0588 (rare historic letters).
   - Its Latin is complete for Latin-1, plus №, €, en/em dashes and quotes.
 - FALLBACK and alternative text face: @fontsource-variable/noto-sans-armenian@5.3.0
   - CSS family: 'Noto Sans Armenian Variable'.
   - wght 100–900, wdth 62.5–100, 100% Armenian coverage.
   - Place it after Google Sans in the font stack so it covers U+055F/0560/0588 on demand.
   - An all-Noto pairing (Noto Serif + Noto Sans Armenian) is the conservative alternative: 135,992 B. The downside is that Noto's Latin set lacks ¤ ¦ ¬ soft-hyphen ± ² ³ µ ¹ ¼ ½ ¾.
 - Suggested stacks:
   - --font-display: 'Noto Serif Armenian Variable', 'Noto Serif Armenian', Georgia, serif;
   - --font-text: 'Google Sans Variable', 'Noto Sans Armenian Variable', system-ui, sans-serif;
   - Set lang="hy" on the html element. text-transform:uppercase works on Armenian.
   - Noto Serif Armenian has no italic, so avoid serif italics or set font-synthesis.

3) FILE NAMING
 - Variable packages: files/<id>-<subset>-<axisset>-<style>.woff2, for example:
   - noto-serif-armenian-armenian-wght-normal.woff2
   - google-sans-armenian-wght-normal.woff2
   - google-sans-latin-wght-italic.woff2
   - Axis-set variants: noto-serif-armenian has wght, wdth and standard. In that package, wdth and standard are the same files and include both wght and wdth. google-sans has wght, opsz, grad, standard and full.
 - Static packages: files/<id>-<subset>-<weight>-<style>.woff2 (plus .woff), for example noto-serif-armenian-armenian-400-normal.woff2. They also have per-subset CSS such as armenian-400.css and latin-400.css. Static CSS families are 'Noto Serif Armenian', 'Google Sans' and 'Noto Sans Armenian'.
 - Armenian unicode-range in all three packages: U+0308,U+0530-058F,U+2010,U+2024,U+25CC,U+FB13-FB17.

4) BYTES (armenian + latin woff2 only, i.e. what a browser downloads for this site)
 - Noto Serif Armenian Variable, wght: 34,636 + 42,964 = 77,600 B.
 - Noto Serif Armenian Variable, wght+wdth: 57,420 + 71,452 = 128,872 B.
 - Google Sans Variable normal: 15,696 + 35,968 = 51,664 B.
 - Google Sans Variable italic: 16,820 + 38,436 = 55,256 B.
 - Noto Sans Armenian Variable: 26,812 + 31,580 = 58,392 B.
 - Totals:
   - Recommended set (serif wght + Google Sans normal): 129,264 B (126.2 KiB).
   - Plus Google Sans italic: 184,520 B.
   - With the serif width axis: 180,536 B.
 - Static weights, armenian+latin: Noto Serif Armenian is about 21 KB per weight (300: 21,680; 400: 20,988; 600: 21,596). Google Sans is about 32–34 KB per weight (400: 31,976; 500: 33,428; 600: 33,680).

5) IMPORTANT PRACTICAL FINDINGS from the Chromium test
 - Google Sans's 'georgian' subset unicode-range includes U+0589 (the Armenian full stop ։). Importing @fontsource-variable/google-sans/wght.css as-is therefore makes every Armenian page also download google-sans-georgian-wght-normal.woff2 (18,088 B).
 - U+2116 № similarly pulls in the cyrillic file (15,964 B).
 - That CSS references 25 woff2 files totalling 965,404 B, which a bundler will copy into dist.
 - Writing our own 4 @font-face rules pointing only at the armenian and latin wght files was verified in Chromium: exactly 4 files were fetched, 129,264 B in total. The test CSS is at (working dir)/research/agents/type/web/fonts.css.

6) OTHER CANDIDATES, rejected or optional
 - Handjet: display/pixel only; missing U+FB16, U+0560 and U+0588.
 - Iosevka Charon: monospace.
 - DejaVu Sans/Serif (@fontsource/dejavu-sans or dejavu-serif@5.3.0): Armenian glyphs are present but there is no dram sign, the files are unsubsetted (253,844 B / 143,920 B per style) and the design is dated.

 - Arian AMU: license unclear.
 - GHEA Grapalat/Mariam: freeware/state property, not OFL, not on npm.
